newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki keeps gains, shrugs off overseas jitters.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki keeps gains, shrugs off overseas jitters.

text.p: Shares closed higher on Friday, shrugging off lower U.S. unemployment data that was momentarily viewed as an inflationary signal, brokers said.

After dipping briefly on the U.S. jobs data late in the session, the FOX stock futures index ended up 0.62 percent at 1,061.80, while the all-share HEX gained 0.59 percent to 3,075.81 points. The FOX ended 1.5 percent higher for the week.
"This won't turn the market," one broker said, after the U.S. May unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent from 4.9 the previous month, pointing to strong growth and possible price pressure.

Bourse-driver Nokia helped the market to a higher close, rising 4.50 markka to 343.50 in solid 107 million markka volume for both A and K-series shares. It accounted for a quarter of the bourse's total 440 million markka volume.
Media group Aamulehti rose sharply after reporting January-April earnings up 59 percent to 51 million markka, beating the median of analysts' expectations for a profit of 43 milion markka.
Aamulehti added 7.50 markka to 180.00 in fair seven million mrkka volume. "The good four-month result will strenghten the share further," one broker predicted. Lift maker Kone
fell 30.00 markka to 620.00 in thin 1.3 million markka dealings after reporting a four-month loss before extras and tax of 19 million markka, versus a profit of 17 million in the year-ago period.
"Kone's results were disapponting ... but trade was not heavy, so I think investors have not entirely lost the faith in the share," one broker said.
Mining and metals group Outokumpu added 1.00 markka to 104.00 in hefty 18 million markka trade, as it continued to draw strength from its interim earnings report released on Thursday, brokers said.
